summary: Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies who taught Shindo Kusumoto and held posts at Ryukoku University, including as full-time lecturer attested in 1987 and attested in 2006.

Hiromichi Kato, born in 1944, works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a graduate student under Ryogon Fukuhara, taught Collett Cox, and held a lecturer post at Ryukoku University attested in 1987.

Hiromitsu Ikuma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Tohoku University by 2019. He has served as a researcher at the Institute of Buzan Sectarian Studies and at Taisho University (attested 2020).
Hiromu Kitanishi (1925–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor from around 1971 to 1991.

Hironari Tanaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies (attested 2015–2020) and held a post at Bukkyo University. He was also a lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Hironobu Minami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Hiroo Kashiwagi, born in 1933, completed his doctoral course at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963) in Buddhist studies. He taught Waso Harada, was president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College, and held posts at Mie Chukyo and Koyasan universities.

Hiroo Sato (born 1953) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1972–1982) and held posts at Morioka College (~1989–1993) and as professor at Tohoku University (~2001–2019).

Hiroshi Aoyagi (born 1957) works in linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from International Christian University (~1984–1986) and a PhD from the University of Southern California (~1992–1998), becoming a professor at Nanzan University around 2007.

Hiroshi Araki (born 1959), a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees including a PhD at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University, Osaka University, and was a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

Hiroshi Arami specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. In posts attested in 2026, he has served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Hiroshi Deguchi (1928–2015) studied at the University of Tokyo and held an academic post at Hokkaido University.

Hiroshi Kanaseki (1927–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1948 to 1952 and held a post at Tenri University from around 1982 to 1998.

Hiroshi Kanno (born 1952) studied at the University of Tokyo in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He directed the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology at Soka University (~2003–2009) and held posts at the Institute of Oriental Philosophy.

Hiroshi Kuroda, born in 1952, is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1974–1976). He served as an associate professor at Osaka Gakuin Junior College (~1985) and Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1983–1990).

Hiroshi Marui (born 1952) specializes in Indology and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo (PhD 2011), Savitribai Phule Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. He taught at Musashino University and the University of Tokyo (1992–2018).
Hiroshi Maruyama works in Indology. He held a professorship at Osaka University and led the Ayurveda Research Society, both attested in 1987.
Hiroshi Nemoto is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed an MA at Hiroshima University, where he also served as professor (attested 2015–2016 and 2026).
Hiroshi Tokushige is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at Koyasan University as a commissioned researcher (attested 2015) and special appointment lecturer (attested 2026).

Hiroshi Yamashita (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied abroad at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).
